bill-belichick.blurb: The press-conference format suits the persona perfectly, the kicking-game read of the half-point loss is a real insight, and lines like "The grade's not playing. jerry-seinfeld.blurb: The half-point cold open comes back in the closer ("nothing turns out to be worth half a point"), and "a rounding error with a trophy" and "the low-talker of losses" are the best jokes of the batch, though a few sitcom references (the double-dip, dating for the apartment) are forced.

william-shatner.blurb: The halting delivery is used as comic timing ("Sixty. Five."), and calling Mitch "the Kobayashi Maru made flesh" plus the Priceline callback on the Matt-Chris tight-end deal give the log real shape past the Trek puns.

abraham-lincoln.blurb: Having Lincoln tell Matt "if you do not want to use the army, I should like to borrow it" is inspired, and the benediction's "find a tight end. Chris has five" pays off nicely, but the dispatches in between are mostly box score read out in a frock coat.

dwight-schrute.blurb: "That is crop rotation" and Joe's LWL form being "the sound Michael makes when he sees a spider" land well, but "the top kicker score in the digest" leaks the source material and the sections settle into a stat-dump rhythm.

theodore-roosevelt.blurb: Using the man in the arena for Chris's half-point loss and "I have negotiated peace between Russia and Japan... surely these two men can negotiate a tight end" are sharp, though the stump-speech voice turns into steady listing in the middle.

john-madden.blurb: The turducken and telestrator motifs hold it together, and lines like "a backfield made of folding chairs" and Henry being a guy you "agree to go to the ground with" feel like Madden, but each game recap follows the same template.

kermit-the-frog.blurb: The Statler and Waldorf asides ("Our act doesn't have a margin. Nobody's ever finished watching it!") give it texture, but Act Five squashes two games together and most of the Muppet jokes are costume, not insight into the week.

arnold-schwarzenegger.blurb: Framing the games as sets is a fair device and "Milk is for babies" is funny, but the recap is mostly a string of catchphrases ("Get to the choppa!", "put that cookie down") laid over an unchanged play-by-play.

chris-berman.blurb: Berman-style nicknames on every player ("Kelce Grammar", "Bo Diddley", "Gibbs Me Shelter") become a groan-count list rather than a story, and apart from the Matt-looking-through-the-buffet-window line it's a standard recap in a costume.
